claims.statement: Spotify issues a Client Secret for each app registered in the Developer Dashboard, shown with the Client ID on the app overview page; the documentation says to store it securely, never reveal it publicly, and to regenerate it with the ROTATE button if compromised.

sources.supports: Client ID, the unique identifier of your app. Client Secret, the key you will use to authorize your Web API or SDK calls. ... Always store the client secret key securely; never reveal it publicly! If you suspect that the secret key has been compromised, regenerate it immediately by clicking the ROTATE button on the app overview page.
The authorization process requires valid client credentials: a client ID and a client secret.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.

openQuestions.question: The pages read state no prefix, alphabet or length for the client secret or for the Client ID, so the candidate is not researched beyond existence. Whether the secret is shown in full after creation is not covered. Corroboration was sought in open-source scanner rule artifacts on 2026-10-04: one artifact was found (the TruffleHog spotifykey detector, at commit 59e3b04e820c4cad30462696ac497853a5f7679c) and none from a second maintainer (the Gitleaks default config at b58d3f102cf3a2c84cb7f923d05c25c9b1aed84b has only a stopword entry; no matching rule was found in Nosey Parker, detect-secrets, Kingfisher or Semgrep rules). One artifact does not meet the two-maintainer requirement, so no tool-corroborated claim is made and the single artifact is only a lead.
